analysis:
Both units are head-side text of docs/provider/cli-reference.md, a documentation-only change. No executable code, configuration, keys or endpoints are modified, so no control is weakened and no trust boundary is moved. I examined the changed ranges in the patch: the waiting_inventory wording (lines 14-16), the autopilot status row (781), the new downloads enable/disable rows (786-787) and the revised Autopilot-set text (821-825).

The docs describe autopilot behavior in which the running provider adds verified downloaded catalog builds to its reported Autopilot set. They also describe Autopilot downloading models on the operator's behalf, on by default while enrolled, with optional limits. This could widen which weights are loaded or advertised, which touches A-004, T-012 and T-027. The documentation says builds must pass manifest or registry weight-hash verification and that the saved selection never grows by itself. It also says ordinary routing cannot load models outside the serving selection.

The actual enforcement lives in source files not supplied here (StartCommand+Autopilot.swift, the model downloader). I cannot confirm that the documented 'on by default' downloads respect hash verification, so the next pass should check that code against the docs if it is in the batch. The logout, revoke and drain text in the unchanged context matches the A-008 and T-053 descriptions. Docs of this kind do not establish deployment or behavior. No finding is warranted from the documentation alone.
